clue.text: A showery trip rearranged? That's commendable

indicators.note: rearranged tells us the letters of the three words before it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A trip spoiled by rain gets an ironic pat on the back as commendable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranged' shuffles A SHOWERY TRIP, twelve letters in all, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonyms meaning deserving approval or credit.

clue.text: Hold up smart family consuming good drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding something up lifts it so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to smart is to sting, as does a nip

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the family word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A stylish family holds up proceedings while knocking back a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' turns NIP into PIN; it looks like a robbery but is a reversal in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink gin is a cocktail of gin flavoured with Angostura bitters, a classic naval drink.

clue.text: A girl's disorientated touring European capital

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the muddled letters surround the next piece
someone disorientated is confused, so the letters of the phrase before it are muddled

parts.note: taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: A confused young woman wanders around a European capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorientated' muddles AGIRLS into ALGIRS, and 'touring' puts E inside it after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Algiers is the capital city of Algeria in North Africa.

clue.text: Rooms, we hear, above entertainment venue — ideal location for a racket?

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places the first part over the next
we hear tells us a word is to be taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: a suite is a set of rooms in a hotel, the plural taken loosely
a spot, as in nightspot, is a place of entertainment

explanation.surface: Hotel rooms over a club make a perfect place for a noisy party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests noise, but it is the tennis or squash bat; 'we hear' turns SUITE into SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet spot is the part of a racket or bat that strikes the ball best.

clue.text: Refrain from taking wife? Sloth leads to virtual estrangement

parts.note: the ai is a three-toed sloth, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: the leads of the two following words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A man too idle to marry slides toward being cut off from his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' takes the opening letters of 'virtual estrangement'.
explanation.definitionFit: To waive a right or fee is to forgo it, choosing not to claim or insist on it.

clue.text: Agent left London gallery a copy

parts.note: a rep, or representative, is a sales agent
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts, a gallery on the Mall in London

explanation.surface: A dealer leaves a London gallery a forged artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction or duplicate of something.

clue.text: Journalist to follow hint describing bent figure?

indicators.note: the journalist piece comes after the hint piece

parts.note: a hunch is an intuition or inkling, a hint of something
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter acts on a tip-off about a crooked character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent figure' looks like a crook, but the definition is literal: a stooped body.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunched means stooped with shoulders bowed, the posture of someone bent over.

clue.text: Attritional conflict when RAF tracer is deployed

indicators.note: troops deployed are rearranged into position, so the letters before are reordered

explanation.surface: Military scene: tracer fire from the RAF in a war of attrition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is deployed' rearranges WHEN RAF TRACER, thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting from dug-in lines, as on the Western Front, wore each side down slowly by attrition.

clue.text: Ambassador excited by special order in hotel that's ridiculously complicated

parts.note: HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
athrob means throbbing, pulsing with excitement

indicators.note: the special order letters go inside the hotel word

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
O is short for Order, as in OBE

explanation.surface: A diplomat gets worked up about a special request at his hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: W Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist known for drawing absurdly elaborate contraptions.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoonist's name became an adjective for absurdly elaborate, improvised machinery.

clue.text: Unusual green with bend close to hole — and ditch

indicators.note: unusual signals the word next to it appears in an odd arrangement

parts.note: a U-bend is a U-shaped bend in a pipe

indicators.note: the close of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A golfer finds a strange green with a dogleg near the hole, plus a water hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges GREEN into RENEG; 'close to hole' gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To renegue (or renege) is to go back on a promise, abandoning or dropping it.

clue.text: Bellicose lot no good in front of house ultimately trespass

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come before the last one

parts.note: an impi is a Zulu regiment of warriors

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A warlike gang worth nothing breaks in at the front of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: An impi is a body of Zulu warriors, a word from southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: To impinge on something is to encroach on it, intruding where one has no right.

clue.text: Ignore retrogressive dope getting dressed down? Not half

indicators.note: going backwards, so the dope word is read from its end

parts.note: gen is information, as is dope

indicators.note: only the front half of the reprimand word is kept

parts.note: to dress someone down is to scold, or lecture them

explanation.surface: Someone told off for scruffy clothes chooses to disregard it, rather emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like British slang for 'very much', but it keeps only the first half of the scolding word; 'retrogressive' marks the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to disregard it or fail to attend to it.

clue.text: Term for describing man entertained by English PM once

indicators.note: the man is taken in, as a guest, by the PM

parts.note: Pitt the Elder and Pitt the Younger were both British Prime Ministers
he is a man, by pronoun

explanation.surface: A former British PM hosts a gentleman to whom a label is applied.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive word or phrase attached to a person, like 'the Great'.

clue.text: German retaining Dutch crew

indicators.note: retaining means holding, so the name keeps the next piece inside it

parts.note: Hans is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A German keeps on a team of Dutch sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands are workers, especially sailors, so the hands of a ship are its crew.

clue.text: Venomous sort possibly fed up about craze? Right

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the craze
possibly signals the words before can take another arrangement

parts.note: a fad is a passing craze

explanation.surface: Someone spiteful, perhaps sick of a fashion, asks if that's right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges FED UP into PUFDE, which goes 'about' FAD.
explanation.definitionFit: This African viper is notoriously venomous, inflating its body when threatened.

clue.text: Superb worker taken with wine in fine college

indicators.note: the worker and wine go inside the fine and college letters

parts.note: F is short for fine, as on pencils
the ant is the classic worker insect
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A first-rate employee sharing wine at a good university.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal synonyms meaning wonderful or excellent.

clue.text: Refined fruit gathered by a Northern type with mechanical efficiency?

indicators.note: gathered by means taken in by, so the following pieces go inside A and N

parts.note: U means upper-class, so refined or posh
a tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: Posh produce harvested by an efficient Northerner.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot-like person acts mechanically, without thought, like a self-operating machine.

clue.text: Pastry later baked during Manx event

indicators.note: during puts the baked letters within the event

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: baked suggests the word's letters are changed, cooked into a new form

explanation.surface: A pie cooked later, in the middle of a motorbike meeting on the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baked' rearranges LATER into ARTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartlet is a small tart, a little pastry case with filling.

clue.text: Complaint over old aristocrat? It derives from rotten matter

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis, is an illness or complaint
a thane was a nobleman in Anglo-Saxon England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A grievance against a former lord turns out to be rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsh gas, produced as organic material decays, is this simple hydrocarbon.

clue.text: Satirical piece inhibited by endless quibbling

indicators.note: inhibited by means held in by, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A lampoon held back by constant nitpicking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inhibited by' finds the answer inside 'endless quibbling', across the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A squib is a short witty or sarcastic piece of writing, a lampoon.

clue.text: Bird getting sun on lake before morning is over

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the morning word reads backwards

explanation.surface: A bird sunning itself by a lake before the morning ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is over' reverses AM, which seems to say the morning has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: The seriema is a long-legged South American bird of open grassland.

clue.text: Unionist is wearing hat for exploit

indicators.note: is is wearing the hat, so the hat goes around it

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A Unionist politician wearing a hat to gain advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tile' is dated British slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit a resource is to make use of it, to employ it.

clue.text: Novelist without energy? No, another

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the energy letter comes out

parts.note: C S Forester wrote the Hornblower novels
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A writer short of energy? No, a different one entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: C S Forester loses E to become E M Forster, author of 'A Passage to India'.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's 'another' means a different writer of novels, Forster being one.

clue.text: Glutton tucking into larder at eleven

indicators.note: tucking into means sitting inside, so the answer is found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A greedy eater raids the larder at eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' sounds like eating but means the answer is concealed inside 'larder at eleven'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel or honey badger is notoriously greedy; glutton is also a name for its relative the wolverine.

clue.text: Test in court a rule by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the phrase is to be taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a reign is a rule, a monarch's period of rule

explanation.surface: A legal ruling seems to put things on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call someone before a court to answer a charge, putting them on trial.

clue.text: Recurrent trouble in payment for car

indicators.note: the reversed trouble goes inside the payment

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property

indicators.note: recurrent read as re-current, running back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Ongoing difficulty in paying for one's motor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reliant was a British car maker, famous for the three-wheeled Reliant Robin.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliant made small British cars, so the maker's name stands for one of its cars.

clue.text: NI voter disrupted noted figure on course?

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Northern Ireland voter upsets a well-known figure in some race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests education or racing, but means a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee Trevino is a famous American golfer, a well-known figure on the golf course.

clue.text: Late speeches ruined race

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Late speeches spoiled the race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges LATE SPEECHES.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase is a horse race over fences and ditches, or a track event with hurdles and water jumps.
